Bigot

BIG-ut -- origin is debated; possibly from an old French term of contempt. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Bigot is a person intolerant of others, especially those of a different race, religion, or background.

The talk show host was widely condemned as a bigot after his remarks dismissing an entire religion.

Worked Example

A landlord refuses to rent an apartment to a qualified applicant for no reason other than the applicant's accent and last name.

That flat refusal to treat someone fairly because of who they are is exactly the kind of intolerance that defines a bigot. Unlike 'critic,' who judges specific actions or ideas, a bigot judges entire groups of people unfairly.

How Bigot Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

chauvinist

chauvinist: a person with an exaggerated, unfair bias toward their own group

zealot

zealot: a person with extreme, uncompromising views

extremist

extremist: a person holding extreme, intolerant beliefs

Antonyms

humanitarian

humanitarian: a person devoted to promoting the welfare of all people

egalitarian

egalitarian: a person who believes all people deserve equal treatment

How Strong Is It? — chauvinist → zealot → bigot

chauvinist vs. bigot

chauvinist vs. bigot: Chauvinist is a bit narrower than bigot -- chauvinist often describes bias in favor of one's own group specifically, while bigot describes intolerance toward other groups more broadly.

zealot vs. bigot

zealot vs. bigot: Zealot can feel more intense than bigot: bigot centers on prejudice against a particular group, while zealot describes an all-consuming, uncompromising devotion to any cause, not necessarily prejudice.

Put it together

Put it together: The exact origin of bigot is genuinely disputed among etymologists -- it surfaces in Old French as a term of religious contempt, with no fully confirmed root beyond that. What is certain is how the word's meaning has stayed remarkably consistent for centuries: someone whose intolerance blinds them to fair judgment.
